subject: chemistry
title: Alkenes: structure and reactions
key_idea: (Separate science) Alkenes are hydrocarbons with a C=C double bond, so they are unsaturated and more reactive than alkanes. They decolourise bromine water and react by addition across the double bond.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers what an alkene is and how to write its formula.

items.meaning: A hydrocarbon with a double carbon–carbon bond, C=C.
Containing a C=C double bond, so atoms can be added across it.
The C=C double bond is the functional group of the alkenes.

blocks.label: General formula of the alkenes
where: n is the number of carbon atoms in the molecule
2n is the number of hydrogen atoms in the molecule

items: An alkene has two fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms.
Alkanes are saturated. Alkenes are unsaturated.
In a displayed formula the C=C bond is drawn as two lines between the carbon atoms.
The first four alkenes are ethene, propene, butene and pentene.
Alkenes have a C=C double bond and the general formula CₙH₂ₙ.
They are unsaturated, so they are more reactive than alkanes.

blocks.text: Bromine water is orange. It is used to tell an alkene from an alkane.

items: Add bromine water to the hydrocarbon and shake.
An **alkene** turns the bromine water from orange to **colourless**.
An **alkane** leaves the bromine water orange.
The bromine adds across the C=C double bond, so the orange colour is lost.

diagram.alt: Pick a hydrocarbon to see what happens to bromine water.
diagram.prompt: Pick a hydrocarbon to shake with bromine water

options.label: Ethane, C₂H₆
options.explanation: Ethane is saturated, so bromine does not add to it.

options.label: Ethene, C₂H₄
options.explanation: Ethene has a C=C bond, so bromine adds across it.

options.label: Hexane, C₆H₁₄
options.explanation: Hexane is saturated, so there is no reaction.

options.label: Hexene, C₆H₁₂
options.explanation: Hexene has a C=C bond, so the bromine water is decolourised.

items: Alkenes decolourise bromine water: orange to colourless.
Alkanes do not react, so the bromine water stays orange.

blocks.text: Alkenes burn and they undergo addition reactions. The functional group decides these reactions.

items: Alkenes react with oxygen in combustion in the same way as other hydrocarbons.
They tend to burn in air with smoky flames, because of incomplete combustion.

blocks.text: In an addition reaction, atoms add across the C=C double bond. The double bond becomes a single bond.

blocks.label: Ethene and hydrogen make ethane
where: needs a catalyst and a raised temperature

blocks.label: Ethene and steam (water) make ethanol
where: needs a catalyst, high temperature and high pressure

blocks.label: Ethene and bromine make 1,2-dibromoethane
where: chlorine and iodine react in the same way

items: The halogens (chlorine, bromine, iodine) add across the double bond to give a compound with two halogen atoms.
In every case only one product forms, because the molecules just add together.
Ethane (alkane)
Ethene (alkene)
In addition reactions atoms add across C=C and the double bond becomes a single bond.
Alkenes add hydrogen to make alkanes, steam to make alcohols and halogens to make dihalogen compounds.

checks.q: Describe the test for alkenes. Give the colour change in the test.
checks.a: Add bromine water. It changes from orange to colourless.

checks.q: Explain why ethene is an unsaturated hydrocarbon.
checks.a: It contains hydrogen and carbon only. It contains a double bond between two carbon atoms.

checks.q: Write the equation for the addition of bromine to ethene.

exam_phrases: (but) ethane does not decolourise bromine water
ethane contains a single C—C bond; (but) ethene contains a double bond

mistakes.wrong: The test is to add bromide.
mistakes.right: Bromide is not accepted. The test uses bromine (water).
Clear is ignored. Say the bromine water turns colourless or is decolourised.

mistakes.wrong: The bromine water turns from colourless to orange.
mistakes.right: The result mark depends on the correct test and the correct direction. The colour change is orange to colourless.

mistakes.wrong: Ethene is a gas and is more flammable than ethane.
mistakes.right: In a comparison of structure, bonding and reactions, physical properties and references to flammability are ignored. Compare the C=C and C–C bonds and the reactions such as bromine water and addition.

worked_example.question:
This question is about the Earth's resources.
Propene is an alkene.

Describe the test for alkenes.
Give the colour change in the test.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the reagent, the starting colour and the final colour. Colourless to orange earns only 1 mark.

exam_phrases: contains a {double / multiple} bond (between two carbon atoms)
A reacts with bromine (water), therefore A is unsaturated

mistakes.wrong: Ethene is unsaturated because it is a mixture of carbon and hydrogen.
mistakes.right: A mixture of carbon and hydrogen, or hydrogen and carbon molecules, is rejected. Say it contains hydrogen and carbon only, and has a double bond.

mistakes.wrong: The bromine water turns clear or is discoloured.
mistakes.right: Clear and discolours are ignored. Say it turns colourless or decolourises.

mistakes.wrong: The bromine water decolourises because an alkene is present.
mistakes.right: Alkene is ignored as a reason. Say a double bond is present or the compound is unsaturated.

worked_example.question:
Compound Y can also be formed in the following reaction
C₃H₈ → C₃H₆ + H₂
compound X compound Y
Explain how bromine water can be used to distinguish between compound X and compound Y.
answer_points: With compound X the yellow colour remains (no change of colour).
With compound Y the bromine water turns colourless.
worked_example.tip: X is propane, a saturated alkane. Y is propene, an alkene, so only Y reacts.

items: But-1-ene has the double bond between the first and second carbon atoms: CH₂=CH–CH₂–CH₃.
But-2-ene has the double bond between the second and third carbon atoms: CH₃–CH=CH–CH₃.
Both have the formula C₄H₈.

exam_phrases: Ethane: bromine water remains orange / orange-brown
Ethene: bromine water is decolourised / turns colourless

mistakes.right: No change is ignored for ethane. Say the bromine water remains orange (or orange-brown).

mistakes.wrong: Ethene: the bromine water turns clear or disappears.
mistakes.right: Turns clear and disappears are ignored. Say it is decolourised or turns colourless.

worked_example.question:
This question is about hydrocarbons.

A student has two test tubes. One contains ethane and one contains ethene.

The student added bromine water to each test tube.

Describe what she observes.

Ethane
Ethene
answer_points: Ethane: the bromine water remains orange (or orange-brown).
Ethene: the bromine water is decolourised (turns colourless).
